title: Contra Partem Donati Post Gesta
author: Augustine

passages.original: Siue ergo exeant, de quibus scriptum est: ex nobis exierunt, sed non erant ex nobis, siue intus esse uideantur, de quibus beatus Cyprianus apertissime loquitur dicens: nam etsi uidentur in ecclesia esse zizania, non tamen inpediri debet aut fides aut caritas nostra. ut quoniam zizania esse in ecclesia cernimus ipsi de ecclesia recedamus — quibus uerbis episcopi uestri nihil omnino ausi sunt respondere, quamuis diu frustra contenderint, quod non in ecclesia praedicta sint figurata zizania, quia dixit dominus: ager est hic mundus nec dixit (ager est ecclesia\'.
passages.english: Whether, then, they go out, those of whom it is written: "They went out from us, but they were not of us," or whether they seem to be inside, those of whom the blessed Cyprian speaks most plainly, saying: "For even if there seem to be tares in the church, neither our faith nor our charity ought to be hindered, so that, because we see that there are tares in the church, we ourselves should withdraw from the church": to these words your bishops dared make no reply at all, although they argued at length, in vain, that the tares spoken of were not figured as being in the church, because the Lord said, "The field is this world," and did not say, "The field is the church."
passages.notes: The closing quotation mark of the edition appears garbled in the scan ("ecclesia\'"); read as the end of the quoted phrase.

passages.original: quam(quam) nec ipsam de baptismo Cypriani sententiam aperte commemorare uoluerunt, scientes etiam illic, si facerent, se offensuros esse naufragium, quoniam Cyprianus non reliquit unitatem et cum eis in illa permansit, qui de hac re diuersa senserunt. unde aut tunc ecclesia perisse dicenda est et non fuit iam, ex qua nasceretur Donatus illorum, aut si, quod uerum est, permansit ecclesia, non in ea contaminant mali bonos, sicut Cyprianus etiam iudicauit, qui cum diuersa sentientibus in eadem uniuersitate permansit. ac per hoc isti se detestando sacrilegio schismatis induerunt, qui propter nescio quorum crimina non probata, etiamsi uera essent, nullo modo se ab unitate toto orbe diffusa separare debuerunt.
passages.english: And yet they were unwilling even to mention openly that opinion of Cyprian's on baptism, knowing that there too, if they did, they would suffer shipwreck, since Cyprian did not abandon unity and remained in it with those who held different views on this matter. Hence either it must be said that the church perished then and no longer existed, from which their Donatus could be born, or, if, as is true, the church remained, the wicked do not defile the good within it, as Cyprian too judged, who remained in the same universal body with those who thought differently. And by this they have clothed themselves in the detestable sacrilege of schism, who on account of the unproven crimes of I know not whom ought in no way, even if [the charges] were true, to have separated themselves from the unity spread throughout the whole world.

passages.original: nam Miltiades iudicauit Constantino ter et Licinio iterum consulibus VI Nonas Octobres. Aelianus pro consule causam Felicis audiuit Uolusiano et Anniano consulibus XV Kal. Martias, id est post menses ferme quattuor. Constantinus ad Eumalium uicarium de purgatione Caeciliani scripsit Sabino et Rufino consulibus IIII Idus Nouembres, id est post biennium et menses prope octo. et idem imperator ad Ualerium uicarium de illorum exilio soluto et eorum furore deo uindici dimittendo litteras dedit Crispo et Constantino iterum consulibus III Nonas Maias, id est post quartum annum et mensem ferme sextum.
passages.english: For Miltiades gave judgement in the consulship of Constantine for the third time and Licinius for the second, on the sixth day before the Nones of October. Aelianus the proconsul heard the case of Felix in the consulship of Volusianus and Annianus, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of March, that is, about four months later. Constantine wrote to Eumalius the vicar concerning the clearing of Caecilian in the consulship of Sabinus and Rufinus, on the fourth day before the Ides of November, that is, two years and nearly eight months later. And the same emperor issued a letter to Valerius the vicar concerning the release of those men from exile and the leaving of their madness to God the avenger, in the consulship of Crispus and Constantine for the second time, on the third day before the Nones of May, that is, after the fourth year and about the sixth month.
passages.notes: The intervals given do not tally exactly with the dates as stated; this is as the text reads. Dates correspond to 2 October, 15 February, 10 November and 5 May.
